subsections.title: Access & sign-in
subsections.html:
The editor isn’t linked anywhere. On the practice site, press and hold the logo for 2 seconds and choose Open or Open in new tab. After your first sign-in, a 📘 link sits next to the site logo in that browser.

How it works
Access key32 characters, checked by the server before the editor opens. Each course site has its own keys.
StoredOnly in this browser, and only once the server accepted it.
Sign outTap your @name in the top bar. Your unsaved work stays in the browser.
Key rejectedSign out, then enter it again. If it still fails, it was revoked: ask for a new one.
Lost keyCan’t be recovered. The admin revokes it and gives you a new one; your published solutions keep your name.

The avatar after your name is the forum identicon of the nickname you use on the main site in the same browser (if you have one).

subsections.title: Writing a TikZ figure
subsections.html:
Write plain TikZ. It is compiled in your browser (TikZJax) about a second after you stop typing.

Real compile, same preamble and colours as the editor. Edit and press Compile (Ctrl+Enter).

Rules

  • Only the \begin{tikzpicture} … \end{tikzpicture} block: no \documentclass or \usepackage.
  • Start with \useasboundingbox. Anything outside the box is cut off, on the site too.
  • Use only the theme colours.

Preamble (added for you)

Included
Packagesamsmath, amssymb
Librariesarrows.meta, calc, positioning, angles, quotes, patterns, intersections, decorations.markings, decorations.pathreplacing, decorations.pathmorphing, shapes.geometric
Macros\dd, \dv, \pdv, \vb, \vu, \abs, \norm (same as in the solution text)

Open Preamble above the code box to see it all.

When something goes wrong

  • A TeX error shows its first ! line and source line under the preview; the full TeX log is below it. The last good figure stays on screen.
  • A compile that runs over 90 s is stopped.

Folding blocks

Long blocks such as \onstep{2}{…}, a \foreach body or a scope can be folded to one line, like in VS Code. Hover the TikZ box: an arrow appears next to the line number where a block starts. Click it and the block shrinks to \onstep{2}{⋯}; click the arrow or the ⋯ again to open it. ⊟ Fold all above the box folds every block inside the picture at once, inner ones too: opening a block shows the blocks inside it still folded. Then the button becomes ⊞ Unfold all.

Sections

Group a long figure into named sections that fold like blocks (like #region in VS Code). Start a section with a comment line of % and five or more =, followed by its name; end it with a line of % and exactly three =. Type section at the start of a line and press Tab to insert both.

% ===== Forces
\onstep{2}{
  \draw[c1,->] (0,0) -- (2,0);
}
% ===

Folded, only the title line stays: % ===== Forces ⋯. Section lines are coloured so the outline is easy to read. Sections can be nested; a section without its % === doesn’t fold. TeX ignores these lines (they are comments), so they never change the figure.

Keep a section around whole blocks. One that ends inside an \onstep{…} still folds by its own arrow, but Fold all folds only the one of the two that starts first.

  • Folding only changes the view: what is saved and compiled is always the full text, and copy / cut copy the full text too.
  • Line numbers keep counting the hidden lines, so they match TeX errors; Go to line opens the block it needs.
  • Backspace / Delete next to a ⋯ opens it instead of deleting it. To delete a folded block, select it.
  • Folds stay when you switch to another problem and back, as long as the text was not changed elsewhere.

Scale (0.25–2, next to the preview) changes how big the figure is shown on the site, without recompiling. Scale and captions travel with the code: copy the whole figure (from \begin{tikzpicture} to \end{tikzpicture}, or all of an SVG) and comment lines go before it, for the scale when it isn’t 1 and for each filled caption:

% scale: 0.80
% caption 2: Weight $m\vec g$ and normal force
\begin{tikzpicture}
…

(SVG: <!-- scale: 0.80 -->, <!-- caption 2: … -->.) Paste that into another problem: the lines are left out, and its scale and captions are set. Pasted captions replace all of that problem’s captions; a figure copied with no captions leaves them as they are. The code you save never contains these lines.

subsections.title: Theme colours
subsections.html:
Figures follow the reader’s theme. Draw only with these names:

WriteBecomesNow
(nothing) or ctexttext colour
c1accent 1
c2accent 2
c3 or cbgpage background
c4 or csurfacecard background

Any other colour (red, blue!40 …) stays the same in every theme and can vanish on a dark background.

Switch the theme (🎨) or day/night: the figure follows. The label’s csurface fill hides the line behind it.

Tip: fill=csurface (or cbg) behind a label knocks out whatever lies underneath, in every theme.

The 🎨 Colors button next to Preamble shows these colours in every theme, night and day.

subsections.title: Steps & captions
subsections.html:
\onstep{N}{…} shows its content from step N on. The highest N is the number of steps (at most 12).

Three steps, each compiled separately. Use ‹ › to step through, as students do (on the site it also plays by itself).

  • Every step gets its own caption field; $…$ works there. Captions are optional, but fill all of them or none.
  • Keep the same box in every step: start with \useasboundingbox. The editor warns when the size changes between steps.
  • \thestep holds the current step number, for anything \onstep can’t do, e.g. \ifnum\thestep=2 … \fi.
  • Step through the preview with ‹ › or ← → (when not typing).

subsections.title: Writing an SVG figure
subsections.html:
The TikZ | SVG switch above the figure box picks how this problem’s figure is written. Each kind keeps its own text, so switching loses nothing; students only see the selected one.

Built instantly by the editor’s own SVG engine. Try changing #f00 to #0a0: a fixed-colour warning appears.

Rule
What to typeOnly the shapes, no <svg …> header. A whole file pasted from Inkscape or Illustrator works too: its header is ignored.
BoxFitted to what is drawn. Type x y width height in Crop box to clip instead (like \useasboundingbox).
CleaningStyles become plain attributes, <use> becomes copies; scripts, images and event handlers are removed.

Colours

WriteBecomesNow
#000text colour (also the default fill)
#f00accent 1
#00faccent 2
#eeecard background

c1–c4 work as in TikZ. Any other colour stays fixed: it is flagged under the preview and before publishing, and can be mapped in Layers & colours.

subsections.title: Layers are steps
subsections.html:
Steps are built from layers: top-level groups. The first in the file is step 1, and each layer adds to the ones before.

The floor is outside every layer, so it shows in every step. “Friction” spans two steps; its label appears at the second.

MarkupMeaning
<g data-layer="Name">A layer. Its name labels the step and its caption field.
Inkscape layersUsed when there is no data-layer.
Any top-level <g>Used when there is neither.
data-steps="3" on a layerThe layer takes 3 steps of its own.
data-step="2" on an elementIt appears at the 2nd of its layer’s steps.
Outside every layerShown in every step.
display="none" on a layerLeft out of the figure (Inkscape’s hidden layers).

At most 12 steps in total. Steps, captions and the step viewer work exactly as for TikZ steps.

subsections.title: States & the state panel
subsections.html:
The pill in the problem bar shows where this problem stands. Tap it to open the state panel.

PillMeaning
emptyNothing written or saved.
unsavedWritten here, never saved.
draftSaved; editors only.
publishedSaved and shown on the site.

The panel also shows the sync state (does this window match the database?), when it was last saved and by whom, and whether the problem has changed since.

ButtonDoes
PublishPuts it on the site. See Publishing & credit.
Save draftStores it for editors only.
UnpublishTakes it off the site; it stays as a draft.
Load from database…Replaces this window with the stored version.
Clear this problem…Deletes the stored solution and empties the fields. Can’t be undone.
History…Earlier versions kept in this browser. See Drafts & history.
Check stateReads the database again (did someone else save?). Your fields are left alone.

Ctrl S saves: a published solution is published again, anything else is saved as a draft. If something needs confirming, a toast sends you to the panel.

subsections.title: Publishing & credit
subsections.html:
Before publishing, the editor checks for things that look broken to students. These are warnings: Publish anyway is always offered.

  • empty solution text
  • unbalanced $, $$, \[ \], \( \), braces, or \begin/\end
  • a caption with no figure step, or only some steps captioned
  • SVG colours that don’t follow the theme, or a crop box that isn’t four numbers
  • the problem changed since the solution was last saved

Publishing waits while a TikZ figure is still compiling.

Who wrote it?

Who wrote this solution?
Shown on the site as “Solution by @name”.
Enter publishes · ↑↓ choose · Esc cancels
Asked on every publish, because one editor may polish another’s solution.
  • You are preselected; whoever is credited now comes next, then every other editor.
  • The site shows “Solution by @name” with that editor’s link. By: in the panel always shows who actually saved.
  • Published and unchanged? The button reads Change credit…: it changes only the name, never the content.

subsections.title: Overwrites & conflicts
subsections.html:
The editor asks before replacing a stored version that isn’t simply your own draft:

When you…Button to confirm
publish over the published versionReplace published
save a draft over the published version (takes it off the site)Unpublish and save
save over another editor’s draftOverwrite
load from the databaseLoad and erase
save after someone else saved meanwhileLoad theirs or Overwrite with mine

Nothing is ever overwritten silently: if another editor saved while you were working, your save is refused and you choose.

subsections.title: Drafts & history
subsections.html:
Everything you type is kept per problem in this browser, so a reload, sign-out or update loses nothing. Other editors only see what you save.

Opening a problem that is stored but empty in this browser fills it from the database.

History…

A version is kept
on every save and publish
before anything replaces the fieldsload, clear, restore
every 10 minutes while you type
  • Up to 30 versions per problem and 400 in total; the oldest go first.
  • Preview compares a version with your window; Restore puts it back (your current text is kept first). Save afterwards to keep it.
  • History lives only in this browser and is never uploaded.

subsections.title: Check all
subsections.html:
Check all (bottom of the problem list) re-reads every stored solution and compares it with the current quiz files.

ReportMeans
published / draftHow many of each are stored.
Problem changed since writtenText, answer or units changed after saving. Re-check, then save.
Only in this browserTyped here, never saved.
No matching problemA stored solution whose problem was deleted from the quiz files.

Click a line to open that problem. It also refreshes the dots, so new work by other editors shows up.
